newsitem.title: USA: Singer Mel Torme returns to hospital.
newsitem.headline: Singer Mel Torme returns to hospital.

text.p: Singer Mel Torme, who suffered a stroke earlier this year, has returned to a Los Angeles hospital for tests, his publicist said on Wednesday.
Torme, 71, was admitted to a Los Angeles-area hospital Tuesday so doctors could monitor some respiratory problems.
"His condition is good and he is continuing his physical therapy in his hospital room and doctors are running some tests," spokesman Rob Wilcox said.

Torme suffered a stroke on Aug. 8 and his recovery was complicated when he contracted pneumonia in August and then in September he had a gastro-intestinal problem. He eventually left the hospital on November 11.
Torme, dubbed "The Velvet Fog" by teen fans in the 1940s because of his rich voice, rose to renewed popularity in the 1980s with an improvisational style and a wide repertory of jazz and pop songs.
Torme was also a song arranger, drummer, actor, author and a writer of tunes, including the classic "A Christmas Song."
In 1982 and 1983, he won Grammy Awards for Best Male Jazz Vocalist for the albums "An Evening With George Shearing and Mel Torme" and "Top Drawer," also featuring Shearing.
